channel.title: Diffbrief · Databases
channel.description: Daily databases stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Garage v2.6.0 adds a web admin UI as v1.x reaches end of life
item.description: Garage v2.6.0 adds a web administration UI, alongside a Helm chart repository release and news about v1.x end of life and a v3.0 beta. The release is useful for teams evaluating an open-source S3-compatible storage system.

item.title: Postgres 19 adds session-level query hints through pg_plan_advice
item.description: The new contrib modules let users guide scan methods, join order and methods, parallelism, and other planning choices without changing SQL syntax or affecting every query. The approach offers a scoped alternative to relying on planner fixes or broad hinting.

item.title: 20TB WD EasyStore prices climbed from $250 to $550, prompting ZFS pool changes
item.description: A 20TB drive that cost $249.99 in 2024 is now listed at $549.99, leading the author to consider moving from ten disks to five and reshaping ZFS pools. The piece connects storage costs to capacity and pool-layout trade-offs.

item.title: Database rows can outlive deletes and commits before pages reach disk
item.description: The explanation covers WAL, older row versions, vacuum and compaction, and how replication and backups fit into row operations. These storage and transaction mechanics are useful background for engineers working with databases in larger systems.

item.title: sqlite3_rsync copies SQLite snapshots over SSH without a local duplicate
item.description: sqlite3_rsync transfers a database snapshot over SSH by comparing hashes of pages or page groups and sending only differing content, avoiding a full local copy. This is useful for SQLite deployments with tight disk space or existing replicas that need efficient synchronization.

item.title: Postgres 19 plan advice cuts a tested join from 405 ms to about 10 ms
item.description: The newsletter reports a test where stored join-order advice takes a query from 405 ms to about 10 ms, alongside coverage of Postgres 19 releases. The result is a useful pointer for engineers tuning query plans, though the item is a newsletter roundup.

item.title: Postgres 19 adds online table repacking and query-plan advice
item.description: REPACK can reclaim bloat without blocking reads or writes until its final swap; new features also include plan advice, replicated sequences, and WAIT FOR LSN. These changes matter to teams managing database maintenance, query stability, and read-your-writes behavior.

item.title: SproutMe cut integration-test time 92.9% by using DuckDB
item.description: Using DuckDB in local development and CI reduced the integration-test step from 10.65 minutes to 0.76 minutes per merge. It’s a concrete example of how changing the test data engine can speed delivery for data-heavy products.

item.title: Mason pairs Postgres compatibility with DuckDB columnar reads
item.description: Mason is presented as an open-source Postgres read-replica using DuckDB, aimed at ad hoc analytics without ClickHouse's query-shape assumptions or SQL differences. The approach is relevant to teams weighing analytical reads against their existing Postgres setup, though the excerpt gives no measurements.

item.title: Arctic lock-free radix tree improves write-heavy RocksDB and Turso benchmarks
item.description: Arctic combines a lock-free adaptive radix tree with a freezing-based coordination protocol and a new memory-reclamation scheme; integrations improve write-heavy throughput by up to 40% in RocksDB and 12% in Turso. The design offers concrete options for engineers evaluating concurrent indexes.

item.title: Sirius adds GPU execution for supported DuckDB queries
item.description: The DuckDB extension runs supported query plans on NVIDIA GPUs, falling back to the CPU for unsupported features; TPC-H tests up to 10 TB report 3.25×–5.50× speedups and up to 79% lower query-time compute cost. The measurements give data teams concrete evidence to weigh GPU acceleration against their current analytics setup.

item.title: A project aims to package Postgres as a single binary
item.description: The project aims to make Postgres easier to self-host by packaging it as a single binary, contrasting its client-server model with SQLite’s embedded, single-file approach. The trade-off matters to engineers choosing deployment models for local and self-hosted software.

item.title: Managed Spark 4.0 reaches general availability with agent-oriented workflows
item.description: The announcement describes MCP-based tools and agentic troubleshooting for Spark pipelines, plus shared table access and governance across Spark and BigQuery. These integrations matter to teams building governed data workflows, though the excerpt provides few performance details.

item.title: gopgext builds PostgreSQL extensions from Go code using TinyGo
item.description: gopgext generates PostgreSQL extension glue and installation files from Go, supporting SQL functions and advanced extension types including index access methods. It runs code inside the database server and is explicitly experimental, making its risks and scope important to evaluate.

item.title: Database Center tests PostgreSQL recommendations on cloned instances
item.description: The preview runs isolated synthetic benchmarks on cloned Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instances to estimate the performance benefit of recommended changes before production rollout. This provides a way to validate database tuning changes without testing on live applications.

item.title: Four probabilistic structures trade exact answers for lower memory use
item.description: The article covers binary fuse filters, UltraLogLog, log-linear histograms and MinHash, explaining their operation and guarantees alongside structures from part one. The comparisons help engineers assess memory-saving approximations for data workloads.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 adds concurrent table repacking and plan-advice controls
item.description: PostgreSQL 19 adds REPACK CONCURRENTLY for optimizing tables without disrupting operations, plus pg_plan_advice for controlling plan stability and query performance. These changes matter to teams maintaining database performance while limiting operational impact.

item.title: DuckDB 2.0.1 LTS adds a native NVIDIA GPU query extension
item.description: The first patch release in DuckDB’s 2.0 LTS line includes fixes and security patches, plus Sirius for running DuckDB queries natively on NVIDIA GPUs. It’s a notable option for teams evaluating local analytical workloads on GPU hardware.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 adds concurrent table repacking and read-your-writes on standbys
item.description: PostgreSQL 19 introduces concurrent REPACK, the pg_plan_advice extension, read-your-writes consistency on standbys and get-or-create behavior that saves a network round trip. These changes matter to engineers operating databases for latency-sensitive and mission-critical workloads.

item.title: Valkey's fbtree cuts sorted-set memory overhead by up to 43%
item.description: Valkey 9.2 replaces sorted-set skiplists with an optimized, high-fanout B+ tree variant; a five-million-member test reports 36–43% less per-member overhead, saving up to 109 MB. The design and measurements are directly useful when weighing data-structure and memory trade-offs.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 adds SQL features and replication improvements in runnable examples
item.description: The hands-on tour runs examples for new SQL features, planner advice and replication against real PostgreSQL 19 servers. Database engineers can explore the changes directly and compare them with PostgreSQL 18.

item.title: Datasette plugin adds streaming Apache Arrow exports
item.description: A new plugin uses Datasette’s output-renderer hook to stream Apache Arrow exports, following the chunked pattern already used for CSV and TSV. Streaming formats can export large tables without loading all rows into memory.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 adds concurrent repacking, planner advice and faster checks
item.description: The release notes list concurrent REPACK, planner-advice extensions, quicker foreign-key checks, adjustable I/O workers and logical replication of sequence values. Database engineers can use the detailed change list to identify operational and performance improvements worth testing.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 adds WAIT FOR LSN for read-your-writes consistency
item.description: A session on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until WAL replay reaches a specific log sequence number before querying, with an optional timeout. This gives applications a practical way to preserve read-your-writes behavior while serving reads from replicas.

item.title: Zerodha shards SQLite to serve JSON blobs at thousands of operations per second
item.description: Zerodha says its distributed SQLite-based Blobasaur serves JSON blobs at thousands of reads and writes per second with single-digit-millisecond latency on commodity hardware. The case offers a useful data point for teams considering simpler storage designs.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 adds online space reclamation, plan advice and replica LSN waits
item.description: PostgreSQL 19 adds REPACK that reclaims space during reads and writes, query plan advice, and WAIT FOR LSN for read-your-writes on replicas. These operational controls matter when tuning and maintaining production databases.

item.title: Data contracts give datasets explicit guarantees for people and AI agents
item.description: Data contracts apply API-design practices to datasets, defining their contents and guarantees as clear interfaces. That can make large data landscapes more robust and give agents trustworthy metadata to work with data autonomously.

item.title: Datasette Lite runs the full Python app in-browser with service workers and Pyodide
item.description: A rewrite runs Datasette in the browser and can load specific releases, repository revisions, SQLite versions, and plugins from PyPI or wheel URLs. That makes it easier to share reproducible demos and bug reports without deploying a server.

item.title: Sutra-OS offers a self-hosted, rule-enforced ontology platform
item.description: The open-source platform models data as typed, linked records changed through server-enforced rules, with numbers traceable to their sources. It may interest teams exploring auditable data models, though the project is an early beta.

item.title: Redict ends development and recommends migrating to Valkey
item.description: Redict’s 7.3.6 release is its last, and its maintainer recommends switching to Valkey with a config-file change for package or container users. Operators running the fork get a straightforward migration path and the project’s rationale.

item.title: DuckDB and an LLM analyzed 2.1 million Amazon reviews with a laptop-built pipeline
item.description: Attendees built a DuckDB pipeline to find products with falling ratings in 2.1 million reviews and used an LLM to summarize complaints; they tested locally on a small sample before running the same files on Hugging Face. The workflow shows how to scale a practical data-and-LLM prototype.

item.title: Aerogramme treats fine-grained IMAP retrieval as a database problem
item.description: The first part of a series examines fine-grained email retrieval and querying in Aerogramme, an experimental geo-distributed IMAP server designed to tolerate network and hardware failures. Its correctness challenges and database framing are relevant to engineers building reliable data services.

item.title: Datasette Apps 0.4a0 adds URL-fragment links between data apps
item.description: The release lets apps read URL fragments and report supported URL schemes to Datasette Agent, enabling one app to link to a record view in another. This provides a lightweight way to compose data interfaces and agent-generated tools.

item.title: PMTiles makes self-hosted map tiles deployable as a single file
item.description: PMTiles packages map tiles in one file that can be served from a storage bucket using HTTP Range requests, with an edge-function workaround for CDNs that do not cache them directly. The approach can simplify storage and delivery for teams seeking to avoid per-load map API costs.

item.title: ParadeDB search joins cut a three-table Top-K query from 2 minutes to 100 ms
item.description: ParadeDB says its StackOverflow benchmark ran a natural three-table Top-K search in 100 ms, versus two minutes in vanilla Postgres, without a denormalized ETL copy. Engineers building search over relational data can weigh that approach against separate search infrastructure.

item.title: Datasette adds streaming row exports and fixes private-query disclosure
item.description: Datasette adds streaming for TSV and CSV exports and fixes a flaw that exposed private stored-query titles and SQL, but did not allow execution. The release combines a useful data-serving capability with a concrete access-control lesson.

item.title: UUIDv4 inserts reach two-thirds the rate of ordered keys in a memory-constrained Postgres benchmark
item.description: The benchmark reports that UUIDv4 inserts ran at two-thirds the rate of ordered keys and generated more WAL; the gap grows as the index outgrows cache. These results help engineers weigh primary-key choices against memory and write costs.
